proposals.title: Adaptive Spatial Normalization with Density-Tailored Graph Clustering
proposals.summary: This proposal outlines an analysis framework that explicitly integrates local cell density estimation with an adaptive normalization method and a spatial neighborhood graph optimized for variable cell distributions. The plan details the use of kernel density estimation to quantify local densities, followed by a normalization scheme that adjusts for these density differences prior to graph construction. The constructed spatial graph will leverage distance metrics that are modulated by local density, ensuring that clustering and downstream differential expression are robust to density artifacts. Rigorous cross-validation and statistical testing will benchmark this approach against standard normalization pipelines, with detailed visualizations highlighting the improvements in capturing intrinsic tissue architecture.

proposals.title: Integrated Density Normalization and Multi-Modal Spatial Graph Modeling
proposals.summary: This analysis plan builds a pipeline that combines density normalization with spatial graph modeling and integrates additional imaging modalities when available. Starting with enhanced exploratory visualizations of raw versus density-corrected expression data, the workflow employs dimensionality reduction techniques tailored for both transcriptomic and imaging data. A spatial neighborhood graph is then constructed to capture true physical interactions, supporting the identification of tissue domains and cell–cell communication pathways. The proposal emphasizes the benefits of multi-modal integration, using gene signature scoring and differential expression analysis that incorporate spatial autocorrelation to validate biologically meaningful patterns.

proposals.title: Benchmarking Density-Adjusted versus Standard Normalization for Spatial Domain Identification
proposals.summary: Focusing on a comparative analysis, this proposal intends to benchmark density-aware normalization methods against standard approaches within spatial transcriptomics. The analysis will involve a quantitative evaluation of local density estimation techniques applied to both two-dimensional and three-dimensional datasets. The workflow includes adaptive dimensionality reduction, explicit spatial graph construction based solely on physical coordinates, and clustering strategies that are directly compared between the two normalization regimes. Detailed statistical tests and visualizations will be used to assess the recovery of known tissue domains and marker genes, underscoring the improvements gained by density correction.

proposals.title: Robust Tissue Domain Analysis via Local Density Quantification and Neighbor Counting
proposals.summary: This proposal aims to refine tissue domain identification by integrating complementary methods for local density assessment, including kernel density estimation and neighbor counting. By contrasting these methods, the analysis seeks to determine the optimal way to adjust normalization protocols in both 2D and 3D spatial data settings. The pipeline will proceed with adaptive spatial graph construction and clustering, ensuring that the chosen metrics capture underlying biological variation rather than artifacts. Comprehensive differential expression analyses and gene signature scoring are planned to validate domain-specific findings, with clarity on how these complementary density measures work together to enhance robustness.

proposals.title: Artifact Disentanglement via Density-Aware Normalization and Spatial Autocorrelation Modeling
proposals.summary: In this analysis, the primary goal is to separate true biological signal from artifacts induced by uneven cell distribution. The framework employs a density-aware normalization method coupled with spatial autocorrelation analyses. Precise local density measurements will be integrated into both the normalization and graph construction steps, while differential expression models are enhanced to include spatial autocorrelation terms. The proposal details a clear plan for metric-based evaluation of signal versus artifact using cross-validation across replicates and multiple tissue regions, ensuring that only robust biological patterns are highlighted.

proposals.title: Benchmarking Computational Frameworks for Uncovering Intrinsic Tissue Organization
proposals.summary: This proposal focuses on a rigorous benchmarking study comparing multiple computational frameworks that incorporate density adjustments in spatial transcriptomics. Enhanced exploratory visualizations will first compare raw and density-corrected data, followed by a systematic evaluation of different normalization and graph construction strategies. The study will integrate adaptive dimensionality reduction and spatial clustering, with each method’s performance assessed via differential expression analyses that account for spatial autocorrelation. Cross-validation across various tissue types and replicates will provide a comprehensive assessment of the strengths and limitations of each approach in uncovering intrinsic tissue organization.

proposals.title: Spatial Domain and Communication Analysis via Combined Density Estimation and Differential Expression Modeling
proposals.summary: This analysis pipeline is designed to identify distinct tissue domains while simultaneously probing potential cell–cell communication. It begins with precise density estimation using kernel density methods and neighbor counting, which guide a density-aware normalization process. Next, spatial graph construction and clustering are performed with attention to integrating physical and molecular coordinates. A key innovation is the incorporation of spatial autocorrelation into differential expression models, which are used to identify marker genes and infer communication pathways between neighboring cell types. Detailed visualization and statistical validation ensure that the derived insights are both robust and biologically interpretable.

proposals.title: Modular Graph Modeling and Differential Testing for Refined Spatial Domain Discovery
proposals.summary: This proposal emphasizes a modular approach, where spatial domain discovery is achieved through discrete, well-defined steps. The pipeline starts with density-aware exploratory analysis and dimensionality reduction, followed by the construction of a modular spatial graph that separates physical from molecular influences. Differential expression testing is performed using methods that account for spatial autocorrelation, and targeted gene signature scoring is applied to elucidate intercellular communication. Each module is independently validated with statistical benchmarks, ensuring that the collective workflow is both interpretable and scalable across diverse tissue types and spatial scales.

proposals.title: 3D Spatial Graph Modeling with Density-Aware Clustering for Tissue Heterogeneity
proposals.summary: Addressing the unique challenges of three-dimensional tissue data, this proposal outlines a focused analysis on 3D spatial graph modeling combined with density-aware clustering. The plan details an explicit methodology for estimating local cell density in a volumetric context using advanced kernel techniques, followed by the construction of a 3D spatial neighborhood graph that adapts to varying density profiles. Clustering is then performed to identify biologically meaningful tissue domains, with differential expression analyses incorporating spatial autocorrelation to validate marker genes. The approach also considers computational optimizations to manage increased complexity, providing an end-to-end framework that robustly captures the nuances of 3D tissue heterogeneity.

plan.user_request: Coordinate domain agents to propose exactly nine computational spatial-omics analyses (without executing them) via draft, critique, and final JSON artifacts.

steps.title: Draft nine spatial analysis proposals
steps.description: Use the Spatial-CV Planning Agent (`spatial_cv_agent`) to read the public background and generate a diverse set of nine candidate computational spatial-omics analyses that are plausible for the hidden paper. The agent must write these as a JSON object to `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json`, containing an initial 'proposals' list of nine items describing candidate analyses, without running any analysis.
steps.reasoning: A dedicated spatial-CV planner is best suited to translate the conceptual background (density-aware spatial statistics, adjacency-based methods, multi-resolution data) into concrete yet hypothetical analysis ideas, providing a structured draft for later critique and refinement.
steps.assignment_rationale: The spatial_cv_agent is explicitly required by the user for step (1) and is specialized for drafting exactly nine spatial analysis proposals, writing them to the draft proposals JSON artifact.

steps.title: Critique draft analysis proposals
steps.description: Use the Critic agent to read `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and generate a detailed critique at `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json`, assessing each of the nine proposals for clarity, feasibility, diversity, and alignment with the background (e.g., treatment of density, adjacency, 2D/3D data, multi-technology support) and suggesting concrete improvements. The critique must not execute any analyses or alter the draft file.
steps.reasoning: A focused critique step provides systematic feedback on the draft proposals, ensuring they are well-justified, non-redundant, and closely matched to the stated methodological aims of the hidden paper before final synthesis.
steps.assignment_rationale: The critic_agent is designed solely for reviewing and critiquing candidate spatial-paper analyses, producing the hypotheses/critique.json artifact without modifying draft or final proposals.

steps.title: Synthesize final nine analysis proposals
steps.description: Use the hypothesis/synthesis agent (e.g., Hypothesis agent) to read both `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json`, then produce the final proposal set at `project/outputs/hypotheses/final_proposals.json`. The final file must be a JSON object whose only top-level key is `proposals`, containing exactly nine items; each item must include only `title` and a detailed `summary` that incorporates critique-driven refinements and clearly describes a hypothetical spatial-omics analysis without executing it.
steps.reasoning: A dedicated synthesis step can reconcile the initial ideas with the critique to form a coherent, non-overlapping set of nine high-quality candidate analyses that best reflect what the hidden paper is likely to have done, in the strict output format required.
steps.assignment_rationale: The hypothesis_agent is responsible for final synthesis of exactly nine spatial-paper analyses and is the only agent that writes the required hypotheses/final_proposals.json artifact in the specified format.

provenance.justification: The user requested a highly constrained three-step workflow with fixed artifact paths and agent roles that does not align with the multi-step paper_hypothesis_generation or other general templates, so a custom minimal plan was created instead.
